reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, full AppointmentResponse StructureDefinition report, deterministic aggregate prepass, relevant R4/R6 AppointmentResponse definitions, R4 maturity map entry, and behavior context reports. Direct behavior findings were absent; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only, not as AppointmentResponse-specific migration burden.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 AppointmentResponse was trial-use/FMM 3, so compatibility matters for scheduling workflows, generated models, terminology-driven matching, and validator behavior. This is meaningful stability pressure, but not the normative/FMM 5 burden; proportionate additive improvements can be acceptable when R4-valid instances remain accepted.

overall.oneLineConclusion: AppointmentResponse keeps its resource identity and has no hard R4-to-R6 instance break; migration is local field, terminology, and runtime handling, so avoidable compatibility churn still matters per change.

reasoning.thesisMd: AppointmentResponse is not a resource-level redesign. The same resource remains, the core participant-response model is recognizable, and the reported structural changes do not make existing R4 instances invalid as R6 AppointmentResponse instances. The important migration work is in local code paths: closed status enums and status business logic, markdown rendering/type generation, recurrence and counter-proposal semantics, and terminology value-set-driven matching.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration shape is mostly stable with local breaks or chores. `participantStatus` adds a new safety-significant modifier status but retains all R4 codes. `actor` widens references to `Group`. `comment` changes from `string` to `markdown` while keeping the same JSON scalar shape. `proposedNewTime` and recurrence fields are optional additions. `participantType` keeps the same element and extensible binding canonical but changes preferred value-set composition. None of these requires a whole-resource migration program before an R4 AppointmentResponse can be represented in R6.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because a resource-level migration program is not already unavoidable, preventing avoidable local breaks remains high-leverage. FMM 3/trial-use does not freeze the model, but it does mean low-cost compatibility preservation should be preferred when the R6 goal can still be met, especially for participant matching and safety/business semantics in appointment scheduling.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The most standards-review-worthy low-cost alternative is for `participantType`: retain the R4 explicit `SPRF`, `PPRF`, and `PART` includes while adding the R6 location-role coverage and `ELOC` exclusion, unless there is a clear rationale for de-preferencing those concepts. By contrast, the richer `participantStatus` invalidation state and native recurrence fields appear proportionate because they preserve R4-to-R6 structural compatibility and address real scheduling needs. The `comment` string-to-markdown change has possible alternatives, but they trade away a computable rendering signal or create duplicate comment fields.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: There are no direct AppointmentResponse behavior findings. Shared Resource/DomainResource operation, search, and HTTP findings can affect generic clients that operate on AppointmentResponse through common FHIR APIs, but they are not AppointmentResponse-specific and do not change this resource's migration shape.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate concluded major migration `No` with `preserve-compatibility-per-change`; I agree with those conclusions. I would characterize the shape as `mostly-stable-with-local-breaks` rather than simply `low-material-change`, because several changes have real runtime, R6-to-R4, terminology, or safety/business implications even though they do not make a resource-level migration program unavoidable.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: The `participantType` conclusion relies on value-set compose evidence because a full expansion comparison was not available from the core package material. Standards follow-up should confirm whether the omitted explicit R4 role concepts are intentionally de-preferred or an avoidable compatibility regression.

findingConsiderations.title: participantType extensible value set composition changed
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the main avoidable compatibility concern and the best evidence for `preserve-compatibility-per-change`. The element, cardinality, type, binding strength, and canonical remain stable, so it does not drive a resource migration program. But the R6 compose no longer explicitly includes R4 `SPRF`, `PPRF`, and `PART`, which can affect terminology warnings, pick lists, and participant-role matching. Keeping those includes while adding the R6 location-role coverage appears low-cost unless there is a specific policy reason to remove them.

findingConsiderations.title: participantStatus required binding changed to a new value set that adds entered-in-error
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The new `entered-in-error` code is safety-significant because `participantStatus` is required and modifier=true. It creates closed-enum, business-rule, and R6-to-R4 handling work, and systems must not treat an invalidated response as active. It is still local rather than resource-level: all R4 status codes remain valid in R6, so existing R4 instances are not rejected.

findingConsiderations.title: recurrence-specific response fields added
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The recurrence fields are optional additions, so they preserve R4-to-R6 structural compatibility. They are important because dropping them in R6-to-R4 conversion can change whether a response applies to one occurrence or a whole series, which is scheduling-critical. Once the R6 recurrence model is accepted, this is a local migration and back-conversion policy issue rather than evidence of broad resource redesign.

findingConsiderations.title: comment type changed from string to markdown
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The wire value remains a JSON string and ordinary R4 comments should remain representable, but generated APIs, validators that distinguish primitives, and UI rendering/sanitization behavior can change. This is a local codegen and display-policy migration chore; the obvious less-breaking designs either lose the computable markdown signal or create duplicate comment fields.

findingConsiderations.title: proposedNewTime added to explicitly mark counter-proposals
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is optional and additive. It clarifies an existing counter-proposal concept without invalidating R4 instances, and R4 already carried the key time information through `start` and `end`. Migration guidance still matters so systems do not infer the flag mechanically when source context is insufficient.

findingConsiderations.title: actor reference target widened to allow Group
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Adding `Group` is a target-list widening that retains all R4 targets. It can affect closed generated reference unions and R6-to-R4 conversion when the new target is used, but it is not an R4-to-R6 break and does not justify resource-level migration.

findingConsiderations.title: Base CapabilityStatement removed several R4 system-level operation advertisements
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared base behavior can affect generic FHIR clients and conformance tooling, but it is not a direct AppointmentResponse behavior finding. It should be handled in the shared Resource/DomainResource and HTTP/API review rather than counted as AppointmentResponse-specific migration pressure.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Review the `participantType` value-set compose change with the responsible work group. If the R4 `SPRF`, `PPRF`, and `PART` concepts were not intentionally de-preferred, preserve them in the R6 preferred set while adding the new location-role coverage.

Publish implementer guidance and tests for local scheduling semantics: handle `participantStatus=entered-in-error`, preserve recurrence scope during R6-to-R4 exchange, and derive `proposedNewTime` only when the referenced Appointment and business context support it.

Update generated-model and UI guidance for local runtime changes, especially `comment` as markdown and `actor` allowing `Group`, while ensuring existing R4 string comments and actor targets remain accepted.
Keep shared Resource/DomainResource operation and search compatibility work separate from the AppointmentResponse resource conclusion so generic API breaks are not double-counted across resources.

caveats: No direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior finding was assigned specifically to AppointmentResponse.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings may still affect generic clients operating on AppointmentResponse, but they were treated as context only as required.

The `participantType` terminology concern should be confirmed with full value-set expansion or work-group rationale because the available package evidence showed compose differences rather than a complete expansion comparison.
